messages:
elaine (prod): Quick thread to align on long-term routing lanes for the platform roadmap. Customers want a spectrum between strict regional isolation and global cost-efficiency. Need to lock specific launch criteria and which customers get what by Q4.

kevin (arch): TL;DR proposal: three graded lanes (Isolated, Preferential, Global) + explicit fallback policy. Differences are stateful routing (KV locality), capacity reservation, and evacuation guarantees. Important trade: stronger isolation >> higher infra footprint + longer cutover.

leo (sales): Customer C and D have legal residency + audit needs. They'll pay for isolated but expect a migration window no longer than 8 weeks. Please bake that into timeline. Also they require contract language about "graceful model degradation".

tara (eng): Implementation notes:
- Isolated lane: pinned regional pools, dedicated node groups, warm KV cache, >95% local-shard hit-rate target.
- Preferential lane: soft pinning with regional preference, cache priming, fall back to global route after 60s.
- Global lane: cost-first routing, opportunistic batching, automatic cross-region failover.

kevin (arch): Suggested measurable launch gates per lane:
- Isolated: infra validation (node isolation test), p95 < 160ms, failover simulated < 180s, cutover docs + rollback tested
- Preferential: p95 < 220ms, regional affinity hit-rate >= 70% under 99th percentile load, canary 1% -> 5% -> 25%
- Global: p95 < 350ms, cost/unit within baseline +10%

elaine (prod): Can we define opt-in semantics for fallback? e.g., for Isolated lane, fallback must be customer-approved for behavior that changes model class. For Global lane, auto-fallback allowed (we lower model size first). Include explicit evaluation hooks for quality drift.

runbot: New doc created: https://go/repo/specs/routing-lanes-guidelines (auto).

tara (eng): Testing & SLOs proposal:
- Canary windows: 72h at each stage for Preferential/Global, 7d for Isolated
- Rollback triggers: error increase >0.4%, latency regression >18%, affinity_eviction_rate >0.5%
- Observability: per-tenant latency histogram, cache_locality_pct, model_fallback_count

leo (sales): Legal will push for explicit "fallback escalation" phrasing. Suggest we use: \"On fallback, Redwood will route to an approved compatible model variant and notify customer within 5 minutes. Customer may opt-out of automated fallback and require manual approval.\" Is that implementable?

kevin (arch): Yes. Mechanically we can gate automated fallback behind tenant flag. We should offer an SLA add-on for Isolated lane that guarantees no automatic model change without permission. Also add metrics to track quality drift: eval_score_delta on a rolling prompt set.

elaine (prod): Action items:
- Kevin: detailed infra + cost delta by lane (spreadsheet) by Wed EOD
- Tara: smoke tests & canary plan prototype by next Mon; include synthetic failure simulations
- Leo: confirm top-3 customers who must be Isolated and start legal template for fallback wording
- Ops: update runbook (pinged separately)

tara (eng): I'll also add a small experiment to quantify warm-cache benefit: measure cold vs warm p95 at 100qps. Expect ~25-40% improvement.

kevin (arch): Migration notes: prefer blue-green for Isolated moves, require KV rehydration strategy (streaming copy), and pre-warm windows. Add a migration flag to console for gradual cutover.

elaine (prod): Meeting set: Thurs 9am to approve lane definitions and pilot list. Everyone bring numbers. If all clear, we target a Preferential pilot in next sprint and Isolated pilot for selected customers in ~6 weeks. :rocket:

leo (sales): Will confirm customer timelines and escalate contract notes.

elaine (prod): Thanks all — concise thread, appreciate the rapid sync.
